name: Akbar the Great
description: Third Mughal emperor, who expanded the empire across most of the Indian subcontinent and pursued a policy of religious tolerance.

name: Wajid Ali Shah
description: Last king of Awadh, a poet and patron of the arts deposed by the British East India Company in 1856.

name: Ashoka
description: Mauryan emperor who, after the Kalinga war, embraced and spread Buddhism across South Asia.

name: Augustus
description: First Roman emperor, who ended the Republic's civil wars and began the Pax Romana.

name: Julius Caesar
description: Roman general and dictator whose career ended the Republic; assassinated in 44 BCE.

name: Genghis Khan
description: Founder of the Mongol Empire, the largest contiguous land empire in history.

name: Kublai Khan
description: Grandson of Genghis Khan and founder of the Yuan dynasty in China.

name: Qin Shi Huang
description: First emperor of a unified China, who standardised writing, currency and measurement.

name: Suleiman the Magnificent
description: Longest-reigning Ottoman sultan, under whom the empire reached its cultural and military peak.

name: Charlemagne
description: King of the Franks who united much of western Europe and was crowned emperor in 800.

name: Cleopatra VII
description: Last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

name: Elizabeth I
description: Queen of England whose reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada and an English cultural flowering.

name: Napoleon I
description: Emperor of the French whose campaigns reshaped Europe before his defeat at Waterloo.

name: Kangxi Emperor
description: Longest-reigning emperor of China, who consolidated Qing rule and expanded the empire.

name: Mansa Musa
description: Emperor of Mali whose pilgrimage to Mecca displayed the empire's extraordinary wealth in gold.

name: Cyrus the Great
description: Founder of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, remembered for a policy of tolerance toward subject peoples.

name: Alexander the Great
description: King of Macedon who conquered the Persian Empire and spread Greek culture across three continents.

name: Ramesses II
description: Pharaoh of the 19th dynasty, a prolific builder who fought the Hittites at Kadesh.

name: Hammurabi
description: Babylonian king known for one of the earliest written legal codes.

name: Peter the Great
description: Tsar who modernised Russia and founded Saint Petersburg as his new capital.

name: Justinian I
description: Byzantine emperor who reconquered much of the western Mediterranean and codified Roman law.

name: Queen Victoria
description: Queen whose long reign gave its name to an era at the height of the British Empire.

name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
description: Founder of the Tokugawa shogunate that ruled Japan for over 250 years of peace.

name: Harun al-Rashid
description: Abbasid caliph whose Baghdad court is remembered as a golden age of learning.

name: Isabella I of Castile
description: Queen of Castile who, with Ferdinand of Aragon, unified Spain and funded Columbus's voyage.

name: Charles V
description: Holy Roman Emperor who ruled an empire spanning Europe and the Americas.

name: Louis XIV
description: The 'Sun King', France's longest-reigning monarch and builder of Versailles.

name: Henry VIII
description: King of England who broke with Rome and established the Church of England.

name: Moctezuma II
description: Aztec ruler at the time of the Spanish conquest of the Mexica capital Tenochtitlan.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
description: Painter, engineer and polymath of the Italian Renaissance, creator of the Mona Lisa.

name: Michelangelo
description: Sculptor and painter of the High Renaissance, who created David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

name: Isaac Newton
description: Physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

name: Galileo Galilei
description: Astronomer whose telescopic observations supported the heliocentric model.

name: Aristotle
description: Greek philosopher whose work shaped logic, science and ethics for two millennia.

name: Confucius
description: Chinese teacher and philosopher whose ideas underpin East Asian thought and governance.

name: William Shakespeare
description: English playwright and poet, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.

name: Albert Einstein
description: Physicist who developed the theory of relativity, reshaping our understanding of space and time.

name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
description: Persian polymath whose Canon of Medicine was a standard medical text for centuries.

name: Johannes Gutenberg
description: German inventor of the movable-type printing press in Europe.

name: Marie Curie
description: Physicist and chemist, pioneer of radioactivity and the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.

name: Charles Darwin
description: Naturalist whose theory of evolution by natural selection transformed biology.

name: Ludwig van Beethoven
description: Composer who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras of Western music.

name: Rumi
description: Persian poet and Sufi mystic whose verse remains widely read across the world.

name: Zheng He
description: Chinese admiral who led vast treasure-fleet voyages across the Indian Ocean.

name: Fall of Constantinople
description: Ottoman capture of Constantinople ended the Byzantine Empire and reshaped Europe.

name: Sealing of Magna Carta
description: English charter limiting royal power, a foundation of constitutional law.

name: Columbus reaches the Americas
description: Columbus's landfall opened sustained contact between Europe and the Americas.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Deposition of the last western emperor, a conventional marker for the end of antiquity.

name: The Hijra
description: Muhammad's migration to Medina, the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

name: The printing press
description: Gutenberg's movable-type press, which transformed the spread of knowledge.

name: Peace of Westphalia
description: Treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, often cited as the origin of the modern state system.

name: Battle of Hastings
description: Norman victory that led to the conquest of England.

name: French Revolution begins
description: The storming of the Bastille opened a revolution that reshaped France and Europe.

name: US Declaration of Independence
description: Thirteen American colonies declared independence from Britain.

name: Discovery of penicillin
description: Fleming's discovery of penicillin launched the age of antibiotics.

name: Enlightenment of the Buddha
description: Siddhartha Gautama's awakening at Bodh Gaya, the beginning of Buddhism.

name: Unification of China
description: The Qin state completed its conquest of the warring states, founding imperial China.

name: End of World War II
description: The deadliest conflict in history ended in 1945, reshaping the global order.
